key_insight: SurgNavAR integrates patient & instrument localization, preoperative image-to-patient registration, and low-latency visualization into a single framework for optical see-through HMDs, enabling a stand-alone AR surgical navigation system. This makes direct, accurately aligned 3D guidance available to surgeons without relying on external tracking infrastructure.
problem_solved: Existing HMD-AR solutions either depend on external trackers or lack robust, low-latency registration and instrument localization, preventing reliable, real-time surgical navigation on optical see-through head-mounted displays.
method: Sensor fusion and inside-out tracking: combine SLAM, depth sensing, and optional fiducials/markers to localize patient and instruments relative to the HMD.
Hybrid real-time registration: align preoperative 3D imaging to the patient using fiducial and anatomy-based landmark approaches with continuous refinement during surgery.
OST-HMD-optimized pipeline: low-latency rendering, occlusion handling, and UI overlays for accurate, intuitive guidance directly in the surgeon's field of view.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, SurgNavAR creates a practical deployment target for models that improve tracking, registration, segmentation, and predictive guidance in the OR, and enables collection of real-world surgical datasets for continuous learning and validation.
visual_elements: System architecture block diagram showing HMD, sensors (depth, cameras), patient/instrument tracking, registration module, and rendering pipeline.
Before-and-after overlays: preoperative 3D volume overlaid on patient skin demonstrating registration accuracy improvement.
Latency vs. accuracy chart comparing SurgNavAR to baseline (external tracker / naive HMD) to highlight real-time performance.
Mockup of OST-HMD surgeon view with instrument trajectory, target anatomy highlights, and contextual UI cues.
paper_title: SurgNavAR: An Augmented Reality Surgical Navigation Framework for Optical See-Through Head Mounted Displays
paper_authors: Abdullah Thabit, Mohamed Benmahdjoub, Rafiuddin Jinabade, Hizirwan S. Salim, Marie-Lise C. van Veelen
